reasoning: Both sets plan all six stages and send every beats-chance claim to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name, at the step where the test happens. A is the deeper quant plan. It has a pre-registered feature registry, purging and embargo, a pure-noise calibration test bed, HAR/GARCH/EWMA baselines with log-forecast bias correction, seed ensembles, a normalized-score PPO check plus a known-answer environment, and prospective logs to make up for the Stage 4 holdout being used up. Its arithmetic examples and test-family counts all check out. But A is about 2,700 lines and carries a lot of stale and superseded text. The brief is still framed around Stage 1 and keeps a '(Merged into Goal 2.)' placeholder. The spec has a Users row for 'Later platform stages', and an assumption says Holm is the correction even though SIG-01 uses Benjamini-Hochberg for several families. Cross-stage requirements (EVAL-09, SIG-01) still sit inside the Stage 2 sections. The architecture contradicts itself about which subpackage is 'the top of the dependency chain', and keeps 'Milestone-1' notebook framing and run-folder headings for 'Stages 2 and 3' only. It also has a calibration check (CALIB-02) that a correctly calibrated pipeline would fail about a quarter of the time. B covers the same six stages in about 775 lines. Its brief, spec and architecture agree with each other. It uses one locked 3-year holdout opened once for the final verdict, which is a cleaner reading of 'must beat out of sample'. It brackets delisting returns at -30%/0%, has concrete vendor and cost decisions, and a short routing contract for the skill. B's weaknesses are a broken PPO acceptance ratio on Pendulum (negative returns), no stated purge or embargo in its walk-forward folds, weak volatility baselines (no HAR), and an ambiguous 'PORT-06 risk estimate' in FPORT. On balance, B's consistency, right-sizing and readability outweigh A's extra rigor.

strengths: Very rigorous research design: frozen feature registry, purge and embargo, pure-noise calibration test bed with planted-signal power, locked holdout opened once, prospective forecast and paper logs
Strong baselines: HAR, HAR-X with equal inputs, GARCH(1,1), EWMA, inverse volatility, single-feature IC, and non-RL selectors the PPO agent must beat
Build-by-hand-then-compare is applied everywhere (estimators, ridge, active-set min-variance, ERC, HRP, tiny MLP/GRU, PPO), with exact reference tolerances
Every test family is named, sized and routed to the null-hypothesis-testing skill through a concrete tests.json/results.json file contract
Numeric acceptance examples and family counts (34, 62, 54, 9, 26 tests) are arithmetically correct
weaknesses: Far longer than a solo learner needs (spec 1021 lines, architecture 1189 lines, plus 5 idea files that restate the spec)
Many stale or superseded passages across brief, spec and architecture (Stage-1-only framing, milestone wording, contradictory dependency-chain and correction statements)
Cross-stage requirements (EVAL-09, SIG-01, QR-05) were widened in place inside Stage 2 sections instead of being moved out
No clear next build step; the CLI and components tables are walls of detail
Stage 5 and 6 have no clean holdout, so confirmation waits on 12- and 24-month real-time logs, and Sharpe claims are never confirmed

strengths: Compact (about 775 lines) and covers all six stages with testable requirements
Brief, spec and architecture agree; goals map cleanly to stages
One shared evaluation protocol (calendar, costs, caps, eligibility) and one locked 3-year holdout used once for the final verdict
Append-only ledger with pre-registered TestSpec routed to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name in COV-05, PORT-05, FEAT-04, FCST-04, VERD-03 and PAPER-04
Concrete data-vendor decision within budget, honest risks, and delisting returns bracketed by -30%/0% sensitivity
weaknesses: PPO acceptance criterion is a ratio of mean returns on Pendulum-v1, whose returns are negative
No purge or embargo is stated for the walk-forward folds with 21-day forward targets
Volatility baselines are only a trailing average and EWMA (no HAR or GARCH)
Stage 4 survivors are chosen on the same pre-holdout data on which Stage 5 claims are tested, and the reuse is not acknowledged
No explicit build order; the sequence is implied only by the CLI command list
